subject: DeltaHealth capacity snapshot & proposed canary path
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@deltahealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: DeltaHealth capacity snapshot & proposed canary path

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking time today. Short recap from our call + concrete next steps so we have alignment.

Key pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes at peak times (400–700ms P95 for inference) that are impacting UX.
- Need strict data isolation for PHI workflows; SOC2 + customer-controlled KMS required.
- Forecasting: +3x Q3 traffic; want predictable throughput and avoidance of noisy neighbors.

Goals we heard
- Guarantee 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints and P95 latency target <= 250ms for health-checked routes.
- Private/reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation and optional burst capacity for batch training windows.
- Clear rollback and canary plan for model rollouts to avoid production regressions.

Preliminary sizing & isolation proposal (high level)
- Dedicated pool: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for latency-sensitive routes; 2 x A100-equivalent for background batch jobs (burstable).
- Isolation: single-tenant pool for PHI routes + network separation (VPC peering) and customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Throughput estimate: ~12k tokens/sec steady-state, headroom for 2.5x traffic spikes with burst policy.

SLA/targets we discussed
- Uptime: SLA target 99.9% (monthly), with 5-minute alerting and a 15-minute mitigation window for failover to fallback model.
- Latency: P95 <= 250ms for pinned routes under agreed capacity assumptions.

Attachments I’m sending
- deltahealth_sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with node counts and cost estimates)
- redwood_canary_playbook_v1.pdf (proposed canary + rollback playbook)

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- Action: DeltaHealth to confirm KMS approach (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed) — owner: Sarah / ETA: Jul 2
- Action: Redwood to share a detailed SOW draft & canary ops runbook — owner: Priyom — ETA: Jul 2
- Action: Technical deep-dive (network + security) with Delta infra — owner: Ben (technical lead) — ETA: Jul 6

If that matches your notes, we’ll turn the sizing file into a formal SOW and route a DocuSign. Happy to adjust sizing if you want a smaller pilot (2-GPU reserved pool) for an accelerated POC.

Thanks —
Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — this is super helpful and close to what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (AWS KMS in our account) for PHI routes. Can you confirm Redwood supports that pattern and whether there are any latency implications for key retrieval?
2) Pilot sizing: we like the idea of starting with a small pilot — 2 reserved GPUs for sensitive routes and a shared pool for non-PHI. What would the expected P95 look like on 2 GPUs under a conservative traffic profile?
3) Cost: can you flag any significant one-time onboarding fees or minimum commitments we should expect in the SOW?

Michael (cc’d) will coordinate the infra deep-dive — he’s our SRE lead. We’re aiming to decide on pilot vs full reserve by next week.

Appreciate it,
Sarah
Chief Product Officer | DeltaHealth

Looping internally — answers / internal tasks:

KMS support
- Redwood supports customer-managed AWS KMS via a cross-account IAM role and endpoint; additional key fetch is cached locally with sub-ms overhead for per-request signing. No material latency hit expected; need security review for cross-account IAM.

Pilot performance (2 GPUs)
- Estimated P95 under conservative profile (60% CPU/GPU utilization): ~270–320ms for single-token RPCs depending on model family (Llama2-13B quantized path). If they pin a smaller model (7B), P95 should fall to ~180–220ms.

Commercials / onboarding fees
- Standard pilot: monthly usage + $7k onboarding fee for private connectivity + 30d SOW negotiation window. If they convert to committed capacity (6 GPUs), onboarding fee can be credited.

Internal next steps
- Ben: prepare technical checklist and security runbook for Jul 6 SRE deep-dive.
- Marissa: draft SOW template with optional pilot vs committed pricing, include crediting onboarding fee if they commit.

Will coordinate with Priyom to send out both docs by EOD Friday (Jul 2).

—Ben
Ben Carter

Great — glad that’s helpful. Quick answers + confirmation of our immediate deliverables: 

KMS: confirmed — Redwood supports customer-managed AWS KMS via cross-account role. I’ve attached the security checklist section that covers key rotation, access controls, and expected audit logs. No expected perf impact; we’ll run a short key-fetch microbenchmark during the deep-dive to show the numbers.

Pilot perf: Ben’s numbers above are our baseline. If DeltaHealth wants sub-250ms P95 on pilot, recommend using a 7B model for the latency-sensitive route during the POC and run quantized weights. We can include that option in the SOW.

Commercials: Marissa will attach pricing + an SOW draft. We will include:
- Pilot option: 2 reserved GPUs, 30-day term, onboarding fee $7k.
- Conversion credit: onboarding fee credited on conversion to 6+ GPU reserved commit.

Deliverables (owners / ETA)
- Security checklist & KMS cross-account guide (attachment) — Priyom — Jul 2 EOD
- SOW draft with pilot + committed pricing — Marissa — Jul 2 EOD
- Schedule infra deep-dive (Ben + Michael) — Ben/Michael — target Jul 6

Links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.company/deals/DH-2026-053) and shared playbook folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DeltaHealth-Playbook) for references.

If everyone agrees, I’ll upload the SOW to the Drive and route a DocuSign with the pilot option so you can start provisioning as soon as we sign.

Thanks — talk soon.
